guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not reacting to Arizona State’s loss to Baylor or BYU’s win over Iowa State as proof of what comes next. The more useful takeaway is that our matchup numbers support the market’s concern about Arizona State sustaining offense. BYU allowed only 80.4 rushing yards per game through five games, while Arizona State converted just 29.6 percent of its third downs through four. If the run game struggles and manageable downs become scarce, Arizona State could have difficulty finishing drives.

We still see a path for Arizona State to remain competitive through the air. Cutter Boley threw for 1,040 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions over his first four games, and Reed Harris produced 499 receiving yards in that span. Arizona State’s receivers also averaged 8.1 yards after the catch per reception, giving the offense a way to create gains without consistently winning at the line of scrimmage.

The problem for us is price rather than identifying the stronger side. BYU’s defensive profile and Arizona State’s offensive limitations support the market’s position, while Arizona State’s passing-game potential creates enough resistance to keep us from wanting to pay that price. With our numbers essentially aligned with the market, we do not see sufficient value to move beyond a pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Arizona State’s passing game against BYU’s pass defense. The run-game matchup points toward BYU, so Boley’s connection with Harris and Arizona State’s ability to generate yards after the catch become especially important. BYU recorded six interceptions across its first five games, meaning Arizona State must create through the air without giving the home favorite extra possessions. For us, that matchup is the clearest route to Arizona State staying within the market’s expectation.

recent_game.fact: Arizona State fell to 2-2 overall and 1-1 in the Big 12 after a 55-19 home loss to Baylor on Oct. 3.
Arizona State gained 409 total yards against Baylor, including 310 passing yards.
Baylor gained 564 total yards against Arizona State, including 244 rushing yards and 320 passing yards.
Linebacker Owen Long recorded a season-high 14 tackles against Baylor; Martell Hughes had eight tackles and two tackles for loss, and C.J. Fite had four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and one sack.
Reed Harris caught seven passes for 125 yards against Baylor, while Omarion Miller had five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown.

opponent_notes.fact: Arizona State is scheduled to play at BYU in Provo on Oct. 31, 2026.
Through Oct. 3, BYU was ranked No. 8 and was 4-0 overall and 2-0 in Big 12 play.

quarterback.fact: Kentucky transfer Cutter Boley is Arizona State's starting quarterback.
Through four games, Boley had completed 78 of 127 passes for 1,040 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions, with 45 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown.
Boley completed 25 of 43 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Baylor.
Boley threw at least one touchdown pass in each of Arizona State's first four games.

offensive_personnel.fact: Reed Harris led Arizona State through four games with 26 receptions, 499 receiving yards and five touchdowns, including three 100-yard games.

Defensive lineman C.J. Fite had started 31 consecutive games and had 14.5 tackles for loss and five sacks in 42 career appearances.

opponent_notes.fact: BYU is scheduled to host Arizona State on October 31, 2026.

quarterback.fact: Bear Bachmeier started each of BYU's first five games and completed 77 of 116 passes for 1,033 yards, eight touchdowns and one interception while rushing for 239 yards and four touchdowns.
Bachmeier passed for 329 yards and rushed for 109 yards against Iowa State, recording the third 300-yard passing and 100-yard rushing game by a BYU quarterback.
Bachmeier had a 162.2 passing-efficiency rating through five games and averaged 8.91 yards per pass attempt.
Treyson Bourguet, a transfer from Western Michigan, was listed as Bachmeier's primary backup and had appeared in two games without a start in 2026.

Freshman receiver Legend Glasker had 19 receptions for 378 yards and three touchdowns plus 83 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns through five games.
Glasker averaged 19.89 yards per reception through five games.
USC transfer Walker Lyons started each of the first five games at tight end and had 13 receptions for 150 yards.
Oregon transfer Roger Saleapaga II started four of his first four appearances and had six receptions for 108 yards, including a 63-yard catch against Iowa State.
Freshman running back Journee Tonga had 91 rushing yards against Colorado State and scored against Iowa State.

Paki Finau started all five games at left tackle, Sonny Makasini started all five at left guard and Bruce Mitchell started all five at center.

defensive_personnel.fact: Linebacker Cade Uluave, a transfer from California, led BYU with 26 tackles through five games and also had 2.5 tackles for loss and one interception.
Defensive end Tausili Akana led BYU through five games with six tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks.
Safety Faletau Satuala started all five games and had 23 tackles, two tackles for loss and an interception.
Defensive tackle Keanu Tanuvasa started all five games and recorded 10 tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss and two pass breakups.
BYU started Jake Clifton at linebacker against Iowa State after Clifton recorded six tackles and a sack at TCU; he added five tackles and two pass breakups against Iowa State.
BYU had six interceptions through five games, with one each by Therrian Alexander III, Hunter Clegg, Evan Johnson, Matthias Leach, Faletau Satuala and Cade Uluave.
